summary: Static four-file review supports the limited process-local receipt-versus-final-publication ordering: preparation is outside the fence, supersession rejects final COMMIT, and existing rollback cleanup remains in use. One guarded-COMMIT cancellation error-classification regression remains. The six fixtures do not establish app integration, durable receipt admission or a hard native-COMMIT latency bound.

findings.claim: Guarded COMMIT bypasses execute's catch-time cancellation normalization. If cancellation arrives after the check at line 80 and COMMIT then fails with a SQLite error, executeUnchecked throws EvidenceStoreError.sqlite and transaction rethrows it after rollback. The previous execute("COMMIT") path checked cancellation in its catch and returned CancellationError for that failed operation. The added precheck does not cover this race.
findings.recommendation: Preserve catch-time Task.checkCancellation around the unchecked COMMIT error path without reinstalling busy retries before COMMIT. Use a test-only SQLite commit hook that cancels the current task and rejects COMMIT; assert CancellationError, rolled-back state and connection reuse from a fresh task. The current six tests do not exercise cancellation on this new path.

risks: Only final publication rolls back on supersession. Earlier staging/snapshot commits can remain and must be invalidated/reconciled by the owner.

Acknowledging the latest revision must cover all earlier pending receipts, through cumulative persistence or ordered draining; a single revision/pending bit does not track independently outstanding batches.
Disabling SQLite busy retries does not bound native COMMIT disk I/O, auto-checkpoint work or time waiting for the receipt lock.
Process-local fencing is not durable inbox admission, startup-gap handling, bounded native callbacks or completed app wiring.
